title: LR disciplinary procedure over joining the Lecornu government ('debauchage')
description: Within roughly an hour of Berger's appointment as Minister-Delegate to the Interior on 26 February 2026, Les Republicains publicly denounced it as a 'debauchage' (poaching) by the Macronist majority and announced the opening of a disciplinary procedure. Per an LR rule adopted on 23 October 2025, LR elected officials who join a government of the presidential majority face party sanctions, including possible suspension. Berger is described as close to LR leader Laurent Wauquiez.
status: Ongoing as of research date; outcome (including possible suspension) pending party disciplinary bodies. This is an internal party-political matter, not a legal or judicial proceeding.
confidence_score: High - multiple press reports and an official LR statement
key_facts: LR announced disciplinary procedure the same day
Basis: 23 October 2025 LR rule against serving in the Macronist majority government
No judicial dimension; presumption of innocence not engaged (party-internal)

title: Panorama 2 / Jardin parisien urban-development project and social-housing demolition in Clamart
period: 2022-2026 (project decisions through September 2025; press investigation March 2026)
description: Critics and opposition councillors accused Berger's municipal majority of conducting a 'casse sociale' (social wreckage) through major real-estate operations. Reporting (StreetPress, March 2026) described the Panorama 2 project as involving the demolition of around 314 social-housing units for a higher-end residential operation (reported as about 516 apartments over four hectares), with a 30 September 2025 resolution said to provide no on-site social-housing reconstruction for Panorama 2. Around 100 families (including 53 social-housing tenants) reportedly faced leaving the Jardin parisien neighbourhood; a 2022 petition to save the area drew thousands of signatures. Opposition councillor David Huynh called the policy 'violent and shocking'.
status: Disputed policy controversy, not a legal proceeding. Berger and his municipal majority defended the projects as urban renewal and security-driven development; figures and characterisations come largely from critical/opposition and investigative sources and should be treated as contested allegations, not adjudicated findings.
confidence_score: Medium - based on an investigative outlet and opposition statements; municipal counter-position exists; no judicial ruling
key_facts: Allegation of net loss of social housing
Contested by the municipality; no court decision
